title: Natural logarithm of a positive real number
statement: For a positive real number $x$, its natural logarithm $\log x\in\mathbf R$ is the unique real number $t$ such that $\exp(t)=x$, where $\exp$ is the real exponential function used in the positive-real power convention [def-weil-real-power]. Thus $\exp(\log x)=x$ for $x>0$ and $\log(\exp t)=t$ for every real $t$. If $x>1$, then $\log x>0$.
